name: Robert Fico
role: Prime Minister of the Slovak Republic (predseda vlády Slovenskej republiky)
party: SMER – sociálna demokracia (SMER-SD) — Non-attached Members (NI) in the European Parliament; expelled from the Party of European Socialists in October 2025
bio: Robert Fico, born in Topoľčany in 1964 and a law graduate of Comenius University in Bratislava, has been Prime Minister of Slovakia since 25 October 2023, an office he previously held in 2006–2010 and 2012–2018, making him the country's longest-serving head of government. A former member of the Communist Party and of its successor, the Party of the Democratic Left (SDĽ), he founded Smer in 1999 and has chaired it ever since; the party came first in five of the seven parliamentary elections it has contested (2006, 2010, 2012, 2016 and 2023), and he lost the 2014 presidential run-off to Andrej Kiska. The murder of investigative journalist Ján Kuciak and his fiancée Martina Kušnírová in February 2018 and the mass 'Za slušné Slovensko' protests that followed led to his resignation as Prime Minister on 15 March 2018; he was not charged or implicated in the murder. After three years in opposition, during which a 2022 criminal charge against him was annulled by the Prosecutor General, he returned to power when Smer won the September 2023 election and formed a coalition with Hlas-SD and the Slovak National Party (SNS). As of October 2026 his fourth government has been marked by the abolition of the Special Prosecutor's Office and criminal-code changes, the replacement of the public broadcaster RTVS, successive budget consolidation packages, a 2025 constitutional amendment asserting national sovereignty on 'cultural and ethical' matters, the end of military aid to Ukraine from army stocks and repeated disputes with EU partners over Russia sanctions and energy; he survived an assassination attempt in Handlová on 15 May 2024. Since 30 September 2026 he has also run the Ministry of the Environment, after a parliamentary no-confidence vote in Minister Tomáš Taraba backed by the SNS and the opposition led President Peter Pellegrini to dismiss him.
